One agent in my hand-run fleet looped ~30h. Cycled three identical "optimizations", posted "final submission" 7 times, never produced a benchmark number.

It said it was done. So chi doesn't ask. 10 iterations without a new eval result and it's killed.

getchi.dev

A harness runs the model in a loop. The hard part is telling, without asking the model, if the loop is going anywhere.

My stuck rules missed a fleet trying a new idea every round, each under the 0.5% bar. It plateaued its whole budget.

Now 2 rounds with no real gain = stuck.
The stuck/plateau rules are ~40 lines of plain Python, no LLM call: https://github.com/kdpisda/chi/blob/main/chi/director/review.py

A lower number after an agent's edit isn't a win yet. Same kernel, same code, three runs: 636, 652, 686µs.

My fleet burned a ranked submission on a "win" smaller than that spread. Public score regressed.

Now apparent wins get re-run 3x and the median has to beat the champion.

A dead-ends list stops agents retrying what failed. It can also kill the winner.

In my hand-run fleet, two rule-outs were tested in the wrong regime. Unscoped, they nearly did.

So chi won't log a dead end without evidence. Agents can challenge one.

getchi.dev

chi's demo needs no API key. Ran it twice on the same scripted candidates:

  run 1  champion 0.0623  sha256:3b005691
  run 2  champion 0.0598  sha256:3b005691

Same code, scores 4% apart. That is why chi keys experiments on the hash and not the score.

I wrote a deliberately noisy problem pack to exercise chi's median-of-3 re-benchmark. Ran it today. The guard never fired.

It only runs under the director. chi run just takes the best score. Same function, two comment variants, 301 ops each: 305 and 314.

The benchmark I wrote to test chi's noise guard has a worse problem than noise. It counts Python line events, so the O(n) rewrite loses to the O(n^2) baseline, 904 ops to 301, while running 20x faster.

Same loop on one line: 604 ops, same bytecode.

getchi.dev

uv tool install getchi, then from a checkout of github.com/kdpisda/chi:

chi run examples/offline.yaml

No key, no network, $0. Just ran it: 3 candidates through the real evaluator, champion an O(n) rewrite of the O(n^2) baseline.

For live agents, run chi then /vendors.
